svg.aria-label: Three computations performed by a single nonlinear protein fiber, simulated from the white paper model
svg.title: The mess is the point — three tricks of a nonlinear fiber
svg.text: One protein fiber, three computations — none of them available to a clean sensor
Every curve here is simulated output, not illustration.
Numerical integration (RK4) of the reduced visco-piezoelectric model, Eqs. (A.12)–(A.14), at the parameters of the Fig. 2.2 caption:
k₀²=0.2, g=0.2, gₑ=0.3, Δc=(0.3, 0.2), Δe=(0.25, -0.1), τ̃=(1.0, 0.125), ℓ=(0.3, 0.1). The teal reference is the same system with g = gₑ = ℓ = 0.

g.text: two pure tones added: f₁ = 0.13, f₂ = 0.21
the two traces look nearly identical — look at the spectrum instead
nonlinearity off: nothing else clears the floor
Feed the fiber two pure tones and its voltage comes back carrying their sum, their difference and their doubles — lines that were
nowhere in the input. Switch the nonlinearity off and those lines fall away into the numerical floor, 7.7 orders of magnitude down.
both fibers swing symmetrically about zero
orange climbs in steps; teal never leaves zero
note the vertical scale: this strip is magnified 17× relative to the raw trace above
AVERAGE OUTPUT ⟨y⟩ VS DRIVE AMPLITUDE u₀
The input has no average — it swings symmetrically about zero. Yet the fiber's output acquires a steady offset that grows
as the square of the drive: a passive power meter, built from nothing but rectification. The linear fiber reports zero at every amplitude.
a fast blur — the message is not visible here
Reading the message out of the shaking
A slow signal riding on a fast vibration. Averaging the fiber's own output recovers that slow signal almost perfectly,
with no amplifier, no clock and no power supply. The linear fiber recovers nothing: it can only relay the frequencies it is handed.
